beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Hussain, and this video is about Muse — Meta's new personal A.I. agent that doesn't just answer questions, it carries out real tasks for you. So I asked Claude: what actually changes when an assistant can act?

output: it plans, browses and pays — not just replies

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — corrects the reel's misconception: Muse as a chatbot that talks -> an agent that finishes tasks.
beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. Muse is not a chatbot that talks about your tasks. It is an agent that finishes them — and your job shifts from asking questions to reviewing what it did.

show.event: 'It describes your tasks.' types, corrects to 'finishes'
'You review what it did.' lands and holds

props.text:

It describes your tasks.

qc.sparse_reason: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW hesitant-writer bookend: the overview is typed token by token, so the 50%/85% samples are partly cream by design. Final frame verified complete: all three lines and both corrections (chatbot->agent, describes->finishes) on screen.

beats.role_note: Answer vs action: the same request handed to a chatbot and to an agent.
beats.narration_text: A chatbot hands you an answer, and the work is still yours. Ask for flights to Miami and you get a list. An agent takes the same request and runs it. It plans the steps, browses the sites, pays with a secure card — and keeps working after you close the app.

show.event: the same request lands in both panels
chatbot replies with a list; 'The work is still yours.'
plans, browses, pays, keeps working — one per spoken step; last step terracotta

beats.role_note: Connected apps: what it can act in, and the model underneath.
beats.narration_text: To act, it needs reach. Muse connects to Facebook and Instagram, and to outside apps like Spotify, OpenTable and your email. Underneath, it runs on Meta's Muse Spark one point three model. Every app you link is one more place it can act for you — so link deliberately.

show.event: spokes draw to Facebook, Instagram, Spotify, OpenTable, Email as each is named

beats.role_note: The four steps: access, connect, ask, review.
beats.narration_text: Using it takes four steps. One: get access. It's rolling out in the U.S. — on iPhone, Android, the web, WhatsApp and a Mac app, with Meta's A.I. glasses coming later. Two: connect only the apps you want it to act in. Three: give it a task in plain language. Four: let it work — then review what it did.

show.event: step 01 lights with platform chips; AI glasses dashed as 'later'
step 03 lights with the plain-language example

steps.head: Connect your apps
steps.body: Email, Spotify, OpenTable — only what the task needs.

steps.head: Ask in plain language
steps.body: “Find flights to Miami under $300 and send me the options.”

steps.head: Let it work, then review
steps.body: Check before you approve — especially payments.

beats.role_note: One task, run end to end, stopping for approval. Generic illustration, captioned.
beats.narration_text: Here's what a task looks like. You type: book me a table for two, Friday at seven. It plans the job, checks OpenTable, finds a table and holds it. Then it comes back to you. Anything important — a booking, a payment, an email in your name — waits for your approval.

show.event: log rows tick: plans, checks OpenTable, finds a table, holds it
approval card rises: Ready to book · Table for 2 · Friday 7:00 PM

beats.role_note: Falsifiability / where it bites: what to check before approving.
beats.narration_text: Three things to check, every time. Payments: the amount and the merchant, before money moves. Emails: read the draft — it goes out under your name. And background work: it keeps going after you close the app, so look at what it actually did.

show.event: card 03 Background work fills; all three hold

items.head: Payments
items.body: Confirm the amount and the merchant before money moves.

items.head: Emails
items.body: Read the draft. It goes out under your name.

items.head: Background work
items.body: It keeps going after you close the app. Check what it did.

beats.narration_text: My verdict. Start with low-stakes errands — music, reservations, drafts. Link only the apps a task needs. Treat every payment as a review, not a formality. The agent does the legwork; the decisions stay yours.

show.event: four verdict lines land in order

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I'm about to try a personal A.I. agent like Meta's Muse. Here are three errands I do every week. For each one, tell me whether to hand it off, what app access it would need, and what I should check before I approve it. Add your three errands underneath. Watch for the ones Claude says to keep — that is where your judgment matters most.
